record_notes.DCP-LETT-1925: July 14, supplied 1856, eight retained blocks, all eleven notes and bibliography read. Asks whether cave animals are specifically American, whether bipolar crustacean genera can confidently be classed northern rather than southern, and for South Shetland fossil wood literature he has not seen. These are explicit requests, not assent to a settled north-to-south migration. Work reread separately from specimens whose location is unknown. Lubbock April marriage and personal news separate. Darwin mistaken report of Dana moving professorship is corrected in later reply, not silently replaced in current prose.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1951: September 8, 1856, all twenty-one blocks, all twenty-four notes, separate Darwin annotations and bibliography read; actual gar-pike tail drawing viewed. July query received a few days before August20–28 meeting, not a precise day. Agassiz/LeConte cave classifications are attributed: fish and Cambarus American, beetle genera not exclusively American, spiders uncertain, Triura only yet known from this cave. Drawing illustrates reported juvenile tail, not a quantitative or universal evolutionary proof. Full later-discovered eight pages are present after formerly published opening; do not follow stale claims that these contents are missing. All bipolar genera/counts and coastline habitat qualification retained; species distribution does not securely identify hemisphere of origin. Kingdom terminology revised, Acadian name history separate. Eights quote is a fragment of carbonized wood, with actual MathML2½ft length and4-inch diameter, not a forest or212ft tree. Family, Lubbock thanks, unchanged New Haven base and future pamphlet follow. Undated Darwin notes and later poor-pamphlet opinion are not Dana body or dated knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1964: September29, supplied1856, twelve retained blocks, all notes and bibliography read. P1–2 directly thank detailed September8 answers, query cave-rat teeth and qualify interest in Agassiz parallelism. Working on book for19years and future publication/first copy remain current plans; single pigeon ancestry and species mutability are Darwin current arguments with difficulties. Negative-evidence PS reports a Bosquet drawing received yesterday, implying September28 for this reported event. Separate September9 reply1952 already acknowledges Bosquet letter and drawings; do not silently redate either or assume one identical delivery, since distinct drawings or date error are unresolved. Political wishes are source prose, with later election result only apparatus. Wishes to see Dana forthcoming paper are not receipt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2016: December8,1856, five retained blocks, all notes and Darwin annotations read. Explicit answer to September29 cave-rat dentition query comes from Agassiz through Asa Gray to Dana, with Dana as sender. P2 directly addresses Darwin doubt and P3 his Chalk barnacle case; routing does not weaken this demonstrated reverse reply. Type-idea argument is Dana qualified theory, not a declaration by Darwin; illegible word remains unresolved. Darwin verso digest belongs to a separate annotation layer and supplies no independent date. No editorial bibliography section present.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2020F: December21, supplied1856, nine complete retained body blocks despite F suffix, all thirteen notes and bibliography read. P1–5 answer missing November28 Dana letter about libration/species, infertility and chemical elements; they cannot be paired with December8. Geological-development paper received/read to some extent, scholarly poor-pamphlet annotation undated. P6 explicitly receives December8 note this morning, and P6–8 answer its cave rat and embryology/negative-evidence discussion plus explain Darwin own comparative method. P9 fresh pigeon request is additional topic. Gray first Statistics paper and Lubbock/Huxley work reported separately; new public descriptions not treated as incoming letters. No earlier activation of December8 source in pre-PS text.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2072: April5, supplied1857, six retained blocks, all twelve notes and bibliography read. Seeks authoritative Dana opinion to test Richardson comparison of temperate versus polar fish distributions against Crustacea, acknowledges scant southern data. Purbeck mammals personally seen at Falconer, whereas prospective Lyell supplement not yet received. Tentative Plagyoulax spelling and mammalian identification are current account, not silently modernized. Lizard importance and Prestwich reaction separate from new mammal classification by Owen; one-character objection qualified despite authority. Gray correspondence broadly acknowledged without a uniquely identified current letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2083: April27,1857, ten retained blocks, all twelve notes and bibliography read. Cold delayed answer to latest April5 letter; formerly unanswered letter is distinct, probably now-surviving December21 2020F, despite stale footnote saying unlocated. Explicit Antarctic reply preserves profound sampling limitation and possible rather than certain same subgenus. All ten geographical arguments and taxa read; MathML latitude35½ degrees, not3512. Source transposition of South/north is recorded in apparatus; adopted text retains source edition, no silent new correction. Absence of observed identical cold-temperate species not universal impossibility. Kinahan criticism distinguishes ecological replacement from proper taxonomic representatives. Stimpson900 species not yet named/results unavailable;1871 loss future. Received Lyell supplement at Dana, with presumed Darwin sender corrected in May25. Purbeck discussion directly answers April5, not January16 list assumed received independently.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2094: May25, supplied1857, five retained blocks, all seven notes and bibliography read. Explicit thanks for Antarctic answer within knowledge limits, newly learned expedition and already-known Stimpson separated. Darwin says Lyell sent supplement, correcting Dana presumed Darwin sender; letter does not itself establish Darwin receipt date. Huxley published outline of lectures distinguished from expected full publication. Lubbock Diptera larval-muscle drawings are body description; later cited1859 moth paper is separate apparatus, not silently substituted taxon. Personal labor constraints and thanks remain Darwin voice.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1960: Additional September23, supplied1856, seven retained blocks, full nine notes and bibliography read. P6 quotes Dana September8 P17 Lubbock congratulations/pamphlet thanks nearly verbatim, proving earlier knowledge than September29 direct reply. Footnote saying this passage is missing is obsolete against complete1951 source, not a reason to discard the match. Lubbock April marriage referenced in Dana quote differs from Diana September11 wedding in P4. Quatrefages review already evaluated, Huxley lectures enclosed, Bantam requested for future chance death. Later pregnancy outcome and publications remain future.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1533: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. September 27 with supplied 1853 year. Borrowed Lubbock Crustacea work for a fortnight, without plates, and read many parts including geographical discussion. Quoted notebook records September 20 completion; distinguish that dated external witness from letter date, without treating missing atlas as read. Own future gift copy not yet known to Darwin. Praises work, requests Lubbock encouragement, hopes to go to press in a month and says thirty plates already engraved; final proof production later. Explicitly says no answer necessary. No incoming cover-letter text.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1534: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. October 10 with supplied 1853 year. On recent London visit found Dana May 4 note with D. D. Owen report at Geological Society, then returned home to find Dana own work arrived. Distinct delivery routes and delayed access; composition date of May note not receipt. Dana title loosely called Crustacea in body, but gifted source identified as separately issued geographical section, not assumed whole two-volume work. Earlier borrowed reading/copying differs from ownership. Owen only illustrations inspected, text not yet read. Earlier September 27 own letter is not incoming prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1542: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. December 6 with supplied 1853 year. Missing Dana letter received about a fortnight ago contains larval homology objections, Lubbock encouragement and other correspondence; no fabricated exact November receipt. Detailed independent Hippolyte/Cryptophialus observations and proposed homologies, forthcoming volume, received duplicate page and confidential assessments of White/Bate/Bell/Baird follow. Lyell journey two days hence is a plan. P6 questions Milne-Edwards new classification and notes temperate maximum, but contains no criticism of Dana Kingdom/Subkingdom geographical terminology. Thus it does not establish antecedent of later Dana 1544. Historical confidentiality and personal judgments remain source prose. Later publications, travel and health outcomes are apparatus.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1544: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Freshly reread full incomplete Dana fragment, including all eight footnotes and bibliography, rather than relying only on prior boundary readings. Open XML lower bound to before December 6, 1855 is editorially assigned from Darwin dated note; substantive reference to printed distribution chapter and Lubbock 1855 paper belongs to later work. P1 includes a cut-off anatomical discussion followed by explicit Kingdom/Subkingdom objection; P2–3 clarifies sections, temperature zones, New Zealand/Australia/America relations, admits Tasmania catalogue gap and regrets terminology. This particular criticism is absent from 1542, whose Milne-Edwards issue is different. P3 Lubbock letter/paper received by Dana, not Darwin; P4 atlas engraved but not out to him. September 1855 English copies and general 1861 availability describe different access facts. Upper-bound note excerpt is not a recovered full missing letter or automatically a full-body Darwin knowledge date. Preserve raw period hold and unresolved exact date; no accepted pair to 1542.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1952: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Additional Bosquet witness September9, supplied1856, four surviving blocks ending mid-sentence, all seven footnotes and full bibliography read. Incoming discovery letter and supplied drawings explicitly received, but absent here. Darwin treats presumed Cretaceous Chthamalus as overturning negative evidence, recommends publication, and qualifies anatomical impressions because out of practice. Actual fossil identification later corrected by Bosquet; later modern record must not overwrite1856 belief. P4 uncertain Lithotrya/carina interpretation and mistaken Balanidae plate reference remain raw with Lepadidae editorial correction separate. No drawing images supplied in this letter source and no complete inbound text for pairing.

visual_readings.visual_observation: Truncated body at left has a row of short vertebral marks continuing into a narrow upward/projecting upper tail lobe; rounded larger lobe below. No scale or labels. Illustrates Dana report of juvenile gar-pike tail and proposed later loss of upper extension, not direct proof of a universal developmental law.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
